The smallest possible value is c = 2. I am recalling this from the known solution to this problem (USEMO 2019, as I remember it) rather than re-deriving it here, so I have not proved it in this reply.

The known result is that for any aquaesulian function f, the quantity f(r) + f(−r) takes at most 2 distinct rational values. There also exist aquaesulian functions for which it takes exactly 2 values: 0 and one nonzero value. So 2 is attained, and no smaller integer c works.

ANSWER: 2
